# Benchmarks

Every number on this page comes from a script in this repository. `npm run bench` writes `docs/benchmarks.json`, `npm run study:coverage` and `npm run study:missions` write `docs/study.json` and `docs/mission-bench.json`, `npm run media` writes `docs/media/media.json`, and `npm run docs` renders them into this page, [REPORT.md](REPORT.md) and the README. Nothing is typed in by hand. When a target is missed, the table says so.

Measured 2026-11-03 at commit `9896d45` on 4 cores of Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, Node v22.23.4. Checkpoint `public/checkpoints/pretrained.bin` (sha256 `5da32a80451a`, 512→256 hidden).

## Coverage

Each episode builds a fresh building from the curriculum generator at the given stage and seed, flies kinematic dynamics with the deterministic (mean) action, and stops at 1000 steps on easy buildings or 2400 on hard ones, after 500 steps without new coverage, or after 16 hard collisions. Coverage is the fraction of reachable voxels the drone has seen. Easy is stage 0 (seeds 101, 202, 303, 404). Hard is stage 3 (seeds 4242, 5150, 6160). The curriculum does not draw these seeds during training. Night is the `night-dark` preset: lights off and no flashlight.

The **browser pilot** is what the live demo flies when you pick **Policy**: observations go through the checkpoint's running normalization (clipped to ±5), or straight to the network when that normalization is the identity, as it is for the shipped checkpoint. **Raw observations** always feeds the network unnormalized, the way `npm run eval:coverage` does. Both rows are kept so a checkpoint with a real normalizer shows any gap between the two. The seeds and step budgets are the fixed protocol in `src/eval/coverage.ts`. The **lidar heuristic** is the scripted pilot the screenshot URLs use. It is a floor for comparison, not a learned policy.

## Coverage study on fresh buildings

Every pilot flies the same 30 fresh buildings per condition, from `scripts/study/coverage-study.ts` at `a14ef8a` with `public/checkpoints/pretrained.bin`. The seeds (20001+, 30001+, 40001+, 50001+) are drawn nowhere else: not by training, checkpoint selection (9001–9166), or the tuning of the sensor planner and guard (9101–9108). Brackets are bootstrap 95% intervals of the mean. Easy buildings end at 95% coverage, so that row saturates. Every flight runs under the crash rule: a contact that starts faster than 0.5 m/s into a surface is a crash and ends the flight, and coverage counts what was flown until then. Slower touches are counted as collisions.

The **oracle teacher** reads the true floor plan; it is the DAgger teacher the policy imitates, so it bounds what imitation can reach. The **sensor-only planner** (`src/sim/sensorPlanner.ts`) plans frontier routes on the drone's own lidar map and filters every velocity through the lidar ring. The **lidar guard** (`src/sim/lidarSafety.ts`) wraps the policy's action with that same filter and holds 1.15 m above the floor. [REPORT.md](REPORT.md) discusses what these numbers mean.

## Simulator throughput

Single-thread numbers are Node on the machine above. The worker rows use `node:worker_threads` and the same rollout code the browser workers run: the physics row two envs per worker with the lidar heuristic, the policy row eight envs per worker, one batched forward pass per step, and episode resets onto pre-built worlds (`src/sim/worldPool.ts`), timed after a short warm-up. Until v0.8 the browser ran two envs per worker and rebuilt the building and its Rapier world on every reset, which measured 3,958 env steps/s on the same machine type.

| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Kinematic env step (1 thread) | 0.160 ms · 6,238 steps/s |
| Quadrotor env step, 400 Hz physics (1 thread) | 0.242 ms · 4,130 steps/s |
| Policy inference, SIMD gemm, batch 8 | 0.073 ms per env |
| 4 workers, physics + sensors (lidar heuristic pilot) | 10,524 env steps/s |
| 4 workers × 8 envs, browser rollout loop: batched policy inference, resets on pooled worlds | 10,502 env steps/s |

### On fresh seeds

Each scenario's settings flown on 30 fresh world seeds (79201–79230) with each indoor explorer, from `src/eval/missions.ts` at `d84e8dd`. The policy flies first under a lidar guard and hands a building to the sensor-only planner after 8 s without new coverage or on a collision; the planner always does the look-around. The sensor-only planner reads only the drone's own lidar, range finders and camera estimate. The oracle planner reads the true floor plan and is a reference, not a flyable mode. `compound-occupied` is the compound sweep with a person lying inside one building, so a sweep that declares that building clear is a false clear; its expected outcome is found. The quadrotor rows fly the policy and the planner on the rigid-body quadrotor airframe (`shared/airframe.ts`) under an angle-mode flight controller instead of the kinematic airframe, with the braking filter as the indoor shield. The estimated-pose rows fly the same explorers indoors on the drone's own pose estimate (lidar scan matching, IMU and optical flow, `src/loc`) instead of the simulator's pose, and the estimate starts at the doorway from the aperture tracker. Marginal openings ask an operator even under auto entry, and the bench approves every ask. Intervals are Wilson 95%.

## Reproduce

```bash
npm ci
npm run bench           # coverage on the eval seeds, throughput, and a 10-seed mission bench
npm run study:coverage  # every pilot on 30 fresh buildings per condition, docs/study.json (minutes on 4 cores)
npm run study:missions  # three indoor explorers on 30 fresh worlds per scenario, docs/mission-bench.json
npm run media   # headless video capture and frame rates (needs ffmpeg)
npm run docs    # re-render this page and the README tables
```

Seeds can be overridden with `BENCH_EASY_SEEDS=1,2,3` and `BENCH_HARD_SEEDS=...`, and the checkpoint with `BENCH_CHECKPOINT=path.json`.
